body.heading: Find a fluffy clock
paragraphs: A dandelion clock is the round, fluffy ball a dandelion makes after its yellow flower. Each bit of fluff carries a tiny seed, waiting for a ride on the wind.
Long ago, children pretended the puffs could tell the time. Count the puffs it takes to blow every seed away — that number is your pretend o'clock.

body.heading: Blow and count
paragraphs: Hold the stem gently and blow with slow, steady puffs. Count each puff out loud. How many did your clock take? Three o'clock? Seven o'clock?
Watch where the seeds go. They float like tiny parachutes. Some land close by, and some sail far away to grow new dandelions.

body.heading: Compare clocks
paragraphs: Find another dandelion clock and try again. Did it take more puffs or fewer? Big, fluffy clocks often take more.
Remember, every seed you blew might grow into a new yellow flower next year. You were helping the plant travel.

takeaway: Blowing a dandelion clock spreads its seeds on the wind, and counting the puffs is an old game.
safetyNotes: Only pick dandelions an adult says are from a clean patch, away from roads and sprays. Do not eat any part of wild plants.
screenFreeExtension: Count how many puffs other things take — blowing out pretend candles, or blowing a tissue across the table.
